name: NORTHWEST BANCSHARES INC
acquired_date: none
notes: Northwest Bancshares, Inc. is the public savings and loan holding company and Northwest Bank is its subsidiary, which is why the Form 5500 sponsor name differs from the payee. The payee is the top of the chain, so the sponsor difference is not a parent. The record's Pennsylvania headquarters and 500 to 4,999 band stand for the FY2022 grant year. The company later announced a move of its headquarters to Columbus, Ohio, which is after the grant year and would move dollars toward Ohio, not away from it.

name: TYLER TECHNOLOGIES INC
acquired_date: none
notes: Tyler Technologies, Inc. is the public parent itself, headquartered in Plano, Texas, and its Form 5500 sponsor and EDGAR name both match the payee. No acquisition of Tyler has happened at any point, let alone before the FY2020 grant year. The record stands.

name: FORWARD AIR INC
acquired_date: none; the entity is the company's own operating subsidiary
notes: Forward Air Corporation's Exhibit 21.1 lists Forward Air, Inc. (Tennessee) as a direct subsidiary, and the same entity appears in its subsidiary lists back to 2012. The parent is in Greeneville, Tennessee and reported roughly 4,500 employees before its January 2024 purchase of Omni Logistics, which came after the FY2023 grant year ended June 30, 2023. The record already shows Tennessee and the 500 to 4,999 band, so nothing moves except the parent name.

name: THE CONNOR GROUP A REAL ESTATE INVESTMENT FIRM LLC
AMERICAN CRAFT BREWERY

The same entity appears in Boston Beer's subsidiary lists from February 2014 on, so it was a subsidiary throughout the FY2024 grant year ended June 30, 2024. name: FirstMerit Corporation
notes: FirstMerit Corporation of Akron was its own public parent during the FY2016 grant year ended June 30, 2016. Huntington Bancshares completed its purchase on August 16, 2016, six weeks after the grant year closed. The record's Ohio headquarters and 500 to 4,999 band stand. The date rests on news coverage rather than the merger filing, so this is a C.

name: Emerson Climate Technologies Inc
acquired_date: Emerson built the Climate Technologies business from its 1986 purchase of Copeland; no acquisition of the payee occurred near the grant year
notes: Emerson Electric's Exhibit 21 to its 10-K for the fiscal year ended Sept. 30, 2018 lists Emerson Climate Technologies, Inc. (Delaware) as a subsidiary, with Copeland Corporation LLC beneath it. That filing covers the FY2018 grant year ended June 30, 2018. Blackstone bought a majority of the business and renamed it Copeland on May 31, 2023, which is five years after the grant and does not change the answer. The Form 5500 sponsor in the input file, Copeland LP, is the post-2023 name of the same plan. Emerson reported about 87,500 employees. The record has the payee as its own parent in Missouri; Emerson Electric is also in Missouri, so the dollars stay put and only the size band moves up.

name: PH GLATFELTER COMPANY
acquired_date: none during the grant year; the company renamed itself Glatfelter Corporation on October 1, 2020 and merged into Magnera Corporation in November 2024
notes: The payee was the public registrant itself, SEC CIK 0000041719, filing as GLATFELTER P H CO during the FY2019 grant year ended June 30, 2019. The same CIK later filed as Glatfelter Corp after an October 1, 2020 name change and as Magnera Corp after the November 2024 combination with Berry's health and hygiene business. Both of those are years after the grant year, so neither changes the answer and the EDGAR name 'Magnera Corp' in the input file is just the current name on the same registrant. One thing the record does get wrong, though it is a headquarters question rather than an ownership one: Glatfelter was headquartered in York, Pennsylvania in 2019 and did not move to Charlotte, North Carolina until 2022, while parents.csv records NC. Worth a separate look.

name: VEEVA SYSTEMS INC
acquired_date: none
notes: Veeva Systems Inc. is the public parent itself, headquartered in Pleasanton, California, with a matching Form 5500 sponsor and EDGAR name. It has never been acquired, so the FY2022 through FY2024 grant years are unaffected. The record stands.

name: CONTINENTAL STRUCTURAL PLASTICS INC
acquired_date: September 2016
hq_source: https://www.f5500.com/ (Form 5500 plan sponsor for EIN 52-2108862 is Teijin Automotive Technologies)
emp_source: https://www.f5500.com/ (Form 5500 plan sponsor for EIN 52-2108862 is Teijin Automotive Technologies)
notes: This is one of the two errors already known to the project, and it is confirmed here. Teijin Limited of Tokyo announced its purchase of Continental Structural Plastics on September 13, 2016 and closed it that month, before both the FY2018 and FY2019 grant years, which ended June 30, 2018 and June 30, 2019. The payee's Department of Labor plan sponsor is Teijin Automotive Technologies, the name Teijin later gave the business, which is the signal that caught it. Teijin employs well over 20,000 people worldwide. The record in parents.csv has already been corrected to Teijin Limited, Japan, so the fix is in place; it stays an 'owned' row here because the input file still carried the payee as its own parent. The source is a trade press account of the deal plus the Form 5500, not Teijin's own filing, so this is a B.

name: AES US SERVICES
acquired_date: none; the entity was formed inside AES
notes: The AES Corporation's Exhibit 21.1 to its 10-K for Dec. 31, 2022 lists AES US Services, LLC (Delaware) as a subsidiary, and the same entity appears in every AES subsidiary list back to 2013. That covers the FY2023 grant year ended June 30, 2023. AES is headquartered in Arlington, Virginia and reports about 9,000 employees. The record already shows Virginia, so no dollars move; the size band moves up.

name: Exel Inc
parent: Deutsche Post AG (Deutsche Post DHL Group)
acquired_date: December 2005 (Deutsche Post acquired Exel plc, the payee's former parent)
notes: A press release filed with the SEC in September 2014 by Griffin Capital Essential Asset REIT II, whose Groveport, Ohio warehouse is leased to the payee, states plainly: 'Exel Inc., a wholly-owned entity of Deutsche Post DHL, is a leading provider of contract logistics in North America.' A 2017 Newell Brands exhibit names the counterparty as 'Exel Inc. d/b/a DHL Supply Chain (USA)'. Westerville, Ohio is DHL Supply Chain's North American office, not a parent headquarters. The FY2018 grant year ended June 30, 2018, more than twelve years after Deutsche Post bought Exel plc in December 2005. The evidence is a third party's description rather than Deutsche Post's own filing, which is why this is a B and not an A, but two independent filings agree and the Form 5500 shows 27,987 plan participants under EXEL INC., far too many for a standalone Ohio company. The record has the payee as its own parent in Ohio; this moves 300,000 dollars out of the Ohio column.

name: CLARIOS LLC
acquired_date: 2019-04-30 (Brookfield bought the business from Johnson Controls)
notes: Clarios International Inc.'s Exhibit 21.1, filed with its July 2021 registration statement, lists Clarios, LLC (Wisconsin) among its subsidiaries. Clarios International is in Milwaukee and the group reports about 16,000 employees. The business was carved out of Johnson Controls and sold to Brookfield Business Partners on April 30, 2019, before the FY2022 grant year ended June 30, 2022. Under this project's convention a private-equity fund is not the parent, so the parent is the Clarios operating group, not Brookfield. The record already shows Wisconsin, so no dollars move; the size band moves up.

name: CARVANA LLC

notes: Carvana Co.'s Exhibit 21.1 to its 10-K lists 'the direct and indirect subsidiaries of Carvana Co. as of December 31, 2022', including Carvana, LLC (Arizona). That covers the FY2022 grant year ended June 30, 2022. Carvana Co. is in Tempe, Arizona and reported about 15,000 employees in 2022. The record already shows Arizona and the 5,000-plus band, so nothing moves except the parent name.

name: Union Tank Car Company
parent: Berkshire Hathaway Inc. (through Marmon Holdings, Inc.)
acquired_date: 2008 (Berkshire took a controlling interest in Marmon Holdings; remaining interests bought by 2013)
notes: Berkshire Hathaway's Exhibit 21 to its 10-K for the year ended Dec. 31, 2015 lists both Marmon Holdings, Inc. and Union Tank Car Company as subsidiaries. That is six months before the FY2016 grant year ended June 30, 2016, so the parent was in place at the time. Berkshire reports well over 300,000 employees. The record has Union Tank Car as its own parent in Illinois; the ultimate parent is in Omaha, Nebraska.

name: Arhaus LLC
parent: Homeworks Holdings, Inc. (the Arhaus group; majority owner Freeman Spogli & Co. through FS Arhaus Holding Inc.)
acquired_date: 2014 (Freeman Spogli bought a majority stake)
notes: Arhaus, Inc.'s Exhibit 21.1 from its 2021 registration statement shows the chain as FS Arhaus Holding Inc. (Delaware), then Homeworks Holdings, Inc. (Ohio), then Arhaus, LLC (Delaware). So the payee did sit under a holding company during the FY2017 grant year. Freeman Spogli & Co. has held the majority since 2014, and under this project's convention a private-equity fund is not the parent, so the parent is the Arhaus operating group, which is headquartered in Boston Heights, Ohio. The record's Ohio headquarters and 500 to 4,999 band both stand; no dollars move.

name: GEORGIA TSS INC (TOTAL SYSTEM SERVICES INC)
notes: The payee EIN 58-1493818 is Total System Services, Inc. of Columbus, Georgia, which was its own public parent through the FY2019 grant year ended June 30, 2019. Global Payments agreed to buy it on May 28, 2019 and the merger closed on September 18, 2019, after the grant year ended. Its Form 5500 sponsor now reads Total System Services, LLC, the post-merger form of the same entity, which is why the sponsor name differs from the payee. The record's Georgia headquarters and 5,000-plus band stand. The date rests on news coverage rather than the merger 8-K, so this is a C.

name: NIDEC MOTOR CORPORATION
notes: Nidec Corporation's Form 6-K dated October 2010 reports that it completed the purchase of Emerson's motors and controls business on October 1, 2010 and that NIDEC MOTOR CORPORATION (USA) 'became Nidec's subsidiaries' that day. That is almost ten years before the FY2020 grant year ended June 30, 2020. Nidec is headquartered in Kyoto, Japan and employs well over 100,000 people worldwide. The record has the payee as its own parent in Missouri; this moves 200,000 dollars from Missouri to Japan.

name: CROCS INC

The record stands.

name: HSNi LLC

name: SIMPSON MANUFACTURING CO INC
acquired_date: none

name: The Home Depot Inc
acquired_date: none
notes: The payee named on the return is The Home Depot, Inc. of Atlanta, the public parent itself. The Form 5500 sponsor, Home Depot U.S.A., Inc., is its operating subsidiary, and JobsOhio's monthly report also names Home Depot U.S.A., Inc. for the two FY2018 projects. The difference runs the other way from the pattern this pass is looking for: the payee is the parent and the sponsor is the child. The record's Georgia headquarters and 5,000-plus band stand.

name: Coldwater Machine Company LLC
notes: Lincoln Electric Holdings announced on December 11, 2018 that it 'acquired Coldwater Machine Company, LLC', and its 10-K for 2018 confirms the purchase closed in December 2018. Coldwater Machine Company, LLC then appears in Lincoln Electric's Exhibit 21 subsidiary lists for 2018, 2019 and 2020. The grant year is FY2018, the fiscal year ended June 30, 2018, which is about six months before the deal. Lincoln Electric's own release describes Coldwater at the time as 'a privately held Ohio-based flexible automation integrator'. So the company was independent when the money was paid, and the record stands.
